awd_titl_txt: Planning: Advancing AI Implementation at Emerging Research Institutions
awd_abstract_narration:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools have the potential to transform and accelerate scientific research and communication. However, realizing that potential in emerging research institutions will often require institutions to invest in the administrative and technical infrastructure, staffing and capacity, required to implement these tools at scale. Many institutions already face structural and resource barriers that hamper their ability to compete for federal and private research funding to grow their research capacity, and the expense of building an AI-supported research infrastructure could exacerbate these barriers. This project will develop the understanding necessary to facilitate the establishment of regional hubs for collaboration on issues related to the implementation of AI in research and research administration. 

To achieve these goals, Ithaka S+R, in collaboration with co-PIs at two Emerging Research Institutions (ERIs), Montclair State University and Chapman University, will convene administrators and research support staff from universities in two regions (in New Jersey and California) to identify and prioritize opportunities and avenues for: a) co-funding software and computing infrastructure, including the possibility of sharing development costs to support engineering and maintenance of AI tools to aid in research administration; b) collaborative professional development opportunities for researchers, research administrators, and librarians or other support providers, as well as possible models for shared staffing and services; c) development of research incubation hubs. Ithaka S+R will publish findings and actionable recommendations for research administrators at ERIs, funders, and other stakeholder communities. The project will seed collaboration in the regional hubs and provide models for communities of practice designed to plan and troubleshoot the expansion of research capacity and competitiveness at regional ERIs,

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Accurate and efficient research administration is essential to the success and integrity of the U.S. research enterprise. Research administrators help universities develop grant proposals, manage awards, comply with legal and regulatory requirements, and ensure that public funds are used responsibly. This work is growing more complex, creating acute challenges for Emerging Research Institutions (ERIs), which typically have small research offices operating with limited resources. 

This NSF-funded planning project examined how ERIs can responsibly integrate generative artificial intelligence (AI) into research administration to strengthen institutional research capacity. Ithaka S+R, in partnership with Montclair State University and Chapman University, organized two regional workshops: one in the greater New Jersey area and one in Southern California. Together, the workshops brought together 63 research administrators, research librarians, IT leaders, faculty, and senior research officers from 26 universities. Participants discussed AI use cases such as proposal review, compliance review, contract analysis, funding opportunity matching, and identification of projects with commercialization potential.

The project identified several shared challenges facing ERIs. Participants expressed concerns about data security, data quality, trust, transparency, reliability, workforce impacts and upskilling needs, and the absence of clear institutional strategies. These findings show that AI implementation is not only a technical challenge. It is also a governance, workforce, and organizational change challenge. Successful adoption will depend on trusted relationships among researchers, research administrators, institutional leaders, IT staff, and technology providers.
